 Services and offices closed this Veterans Day in the Valley 
 During the closure, residents can still access a variety of DMV services online through PennDOT's website, including forms, publications, and driver’s training manuals. 
 By Zach Mosca, Multimedia Producer

 MAHONING & SHENANGO VALLEY - Wednesday is Veteran’s Day, which means several federal, state and local offices and services will be closed for the day. Here’s everything you need to know.
 All U.S. Post Offices close on Veterans Day, so the USPS will not deliver mail anywhere in the U.S. on Wednesday.
 Some self-service options are still available via kiosks in select lobbies, including postage printing for Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express and international shipping, stamps for purchase, the ability to weigh and mail packages and package tracking information.
 You can also access a variety of services on USPS’s website like purchasing stamps, holding your mail, changing your address and more.
 Banks are also closed, but most still offer ATM access for withdrawals, as well as online banking.
 All local courthouses will also be closed for the holiday. Some courthouses image online records, so residents can still view court documents or case dockets.
 Ohio and Pennsylvania’s driver’s license centers are also closed, with both offering certain services online depending on where you live.
 In Ohio, online services include:
 Applying for a driver’s license, state ID card or commercial driver’s license renewal or reprint
 Renewing your registration
 Replacing your license plates
 Online driver’s permit testing
 Scheduling your driver’s test
 Online title transfers
 Changing your address
 In Pennsylvania, online services include:
 License and registration renewal
 Applying for a Real ID
 Checking personalized license plate availability
 Applying for a disability placard
 Paying user fees
 Changing your address
 Scheduling your driver’s test
